thread:
ana: RFC follow-up: propose resource-scoped API keys for model-serving endpoints. goal: smaller blast radius for CI & infra, and cheaper fast-path checks. thoughts? :mag:

ben: what do you mean by fast-path checks? are we avoiding authz policy evals entirely?

diane: idea: token contains an embedded allow-list of resource IDs + a small issuer claim. validate signature locally and short-circuit deny if resource not in list. still run full RBAC when token allows the resource. keeps deny path cheap.

omar: that helps latency. runtime cost is crypto verify + parse. need to bench for p99. also decide signature scheme: HMAC vs ed25519. HMAC means shared secret on many servers; ed25519 lets us rotate keys and avoid secret distribution.

ana: leaning ed25519 with compact base64 payload. token format suggestion: <kid>.<b64claims>.<sig>. claims example: {"kid":"ak_7","sub":"svc:xxx","res":["proj:77","proj:77/model:abc"],"exp":1723530000}

ben: revocation is the tricky part. signed tokens are long-lived otherwise. we can keep fairly short TTLs (1-4h) and maintain an exception revocation set for immediate disables. maybe a bloom-filter backed cache that is loaded into memory for quick checks.

diane: bloom filter is probabilistic; false positives cause denies which is bad. prefer two-tier: in-memory LRU with Redis fallback for misses. avoid DB per-request.

omar: RBAC interplay: tokens define resource scope, but roles/permissions still come from principal bindings. implement as: if token has resource scope, check resource ∈ token -> then evaluate role bindings for principal. If resource not in token -> deny (no policy eval). If token empty -> full RBAC.

ana: exactly. also include original api_key_id and creator in claims so audit logs map back: claim names: "kid", "creator", "res".

ben: migration: accept both opaque and signed tokens for 9 months. default new console keys to signed short-lived. offer an exchange endpoint so CI can swap long-lived opaque -> short-lived signed. log exchanges for audits.

diane: SDKs should implement the exchange flow and auto-refresh signed tokens. that prevents users from pasting long-lived secrets into CI.

omar: SLO concerns: need ENG-SRE to confirm verify crypto cost at scale and ensure hot paths (embeddings small requests) aren't regressing. also monitor cold-start of revocation cache.

ana: next steps: 1) write short RFC with token schema + migration timeline 2) bench verifier lib (ed25519) + memcache design 3) small canary deploy with 1% traffic and telemetry hooks 4) SDK + console changes 5) run migration metrics after 3 months and iterate.

ben: security note: rotate issuer keys monthly and provide key discovery endpoint (/auth/issuers). cache keys for short TTLs.

diane: operational note: add an endpoint GET /auth/scope-info that returns token claims without performing action; useful for CI and debugging.

omar: engineering tasks: A) ed25519 verifier library + audit B) revocation cache + admission path C) exchange endpoint + audit logs D) SDK refresh support.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: auth-service/resource-scope-canary (canary 1% -> 5%) in 8m :rocket:

ana: assign tasks and I'll draft the RFC and invite eng-sre & eng-platform. meeting next Wed to walk the design.
